stories.title: Unsold homes up 12% even as top-seven sales cross a lakh
stories.summary: ANAROCK's Q3 2026 view shows about 1,00,200 homes sold across India's top seven cities in July to September, while available inventory rose 12% year on year to around 6,30,600 units. Demand recovered. The stock pile grew faster.

stories.title: Bengaluru office rents rise 11.5%, level with Tokyo
stories.summary: Knight Frank's Asia-Pacific office report for Q3 2026 puts Bengaluru's prime office rent growth at 11.5% year on year, matching Tokyo among 24 markets tracked. Mumbai leasing jumped 33% in the quarter. Startup City is pricing like somewhere that invents robots.

stories.title: Office leasing down 13.6% in three cities as rents still climb
stories.summary: Knight Frank says combined office leasing across Bengaluru, Mumbai and Delhi-NCR fell 13.6% year on year in Q3 2026 to 7.6 million sq ft, while prime rents rose about 7.5% on average. Less space taken. Higher asking rents. The spreadsheet is conflicted.

stories.title: Bengaluru and Hyderabad double fresh office supply, JLL says
stories.summary: JLL India reports fresh office supply in Bengaluru and Hyderabad rose to 30.45 million sq ft in January to September, double the year-ago pace, as top-seven cities reached 43.66 million sq ft overall. Only those two cities added more new space.

stories.title: Mumbai luxury homes average 17 sales a day in H1 FY27
stories.summary: A Lighthouse Luxury and Zapkey report says Mumbai recorded more than 17 daily sales of homes priced at ₹5 crore and above in April to September 2026, with 3,145 luxury properties worth ₹326.23 billion registered. Q2 outpaced Q1 on both count and value.

stories.title: M3M plans 10 million sq ft of branded residences by year end
stories.summary: M3M India says it aims to expand its branded residential portfolio from about 6.9 million sq ft to 10 million sq ft by end-2026, targeting an extra ₹13,400 crore of topline, and has launched an invitation-only M3M Black Circle privilege platform for buyers.

stories.title: Aqua Line lifts Marol rents toward Lokhandwala levels
stories.summary: Mumbai Mirror reports furnished 1BHK rents near Marol Naka reaching up to ₹70,000 a month as Aqua Line metro links pull Nariman Point and BKC workers east. Agents say Andheri East is closing the gap with Lokhandwala. The station did what the brochure promised.

stories.title: Knight Frank: Bengaluru leads India on office rent growth
stories.summary: A Knight Frank Asia-Pacific note says Bengaluru recorded 11.5% year-on-year growth in prime office rents in Q3 2026, matching Tokyo, while Mumbai rose 4% and Delhi-NCR 5.4%. Across the region, prime rents were up 1% quarter on quarter.

stories.title: NBCC Avenue Towers e-auction fetches ₹5,191 crore record
stories.summary: NBCC's e-auction of Avenue Towers residential units on New Delhi's Africa Avenue raised ₹5,191 crore, its highest single residential e-auction, at an average about ₹59,014 per sq ft, nearly 59% above reserve. Public sector inventory found private sector prices.

stories.title: Blackstone opens Bengaluru GCC as India's biggest landlord
stories.summary: Blackstone opened a Global Capability Center in Bengaluru, its second India base, backing worldwide fund operations. The firm is already India's largest owner of office, retail and logistics real estate and helped launch five of six listed REITs. The landlord now has a second office for its own staff.

stories.title: Gurugram excavation risk: Sector 31 building tilts beside dig
stories.summary: Hindustan Times reports a four-storey home in Gurugram Sector 31 cracked and tilted toward an adjoining excavation, with four families evacuated and notices issued to neighbours after inch-wide cracks. Work on the next plot was halted. The soil is making its own planning notes.

stories.title: Bombay HC tells ED to clear NOC for stalled society rebuild
stories.summary: The Bombay High Court directed the Enforcement Directorate to issue a no-objection certificate within six weeks so a 44-year-old Mumbai housing society can appoint a developer, saying safeguards can protect the agency's interest in a replacement flat after one unit was attached.

stories.title: Gen Z buyers want smart locks, finished homes, faster keys
stories.summary: A BASIC Home Loan survey cited by the Times of India says the average home-loan applicant age has fallen to 25, with millennials and Gen Z near 90% of residential acquisitions. Younger buyers want ready interiors and possession without the long wait. The wishlist includes Instagram lighting.

stories.title: Haryana RERA: occupation certificate alone is not possession
stories.summary: Haryana RERA, Gurugram, held that an offer of possession is valid only if the developer has an occupation certificate, the flat is habitable, and the offer is free of unreasonable extra demands. Member Phool Singh Saini directed Godrej Real View Developers to pay delayed possession interest.

stories.title: Rent versus buy: the EMI is not the full cost of ownership
stories.summary: Outlook Money walks through why rising prices and home-loan rates make renting rational for some households when ownership costs go beyond the EMI and money left in other investments can compound. The old line that rent is wasted money gets a spreadsheet challenge.

stories.title: GDA eyes year-end Harnandipuram launch once RERA clears
stories.summary: Ghaziabad Development Authority officials told Hindustan Times that phase 1 of the Harnandipuram township near Raj Nagar Extension may launch by December, once RERA approval arrives for the roughly 501-hectare project across eight villages. Authority projects usually move faster. They are waiting anyway.

stories.title: TG RERA freezes two Sri Laxmi Estates plots after unpaid registration
stories.summary: Telangana RERA restrained Sri Laxmi Estates and others from dealing with two plots after a buyer said she paid ₹6 lakh under a January 2024 agreement but never got registration in Kalpatharuvu-3 at Bachannapeta. The interim order blocks further dealing in the disputed plots.

stories.title: NRI to NRI property sales: tax rules still need careful paperwork
stories.summary: Moneycontrol outlines tax points when one NRI sells property to another NRI, covering TDS and repatriation basics that trip up cross-border deals. The registry office is local. The tax residency tests are not.

stories.title: Ashiana signs Gurugram senior-living JDA with ₹1,300 crore potential
stories.summary: Ashiana Housing disclosed a joint development agreement for a senior-living project on about 4.4125 acres in Sector 78, Gurugram, with approximate sales potential of ₹1,300 crore under SEBI LODR filings dated 29 October 2026. Retirement housing is getting a Sector 78 pin.

stories.title: Noida Master Plan tweak may free long-pending farmer plots
stories.summary: Noida Authority amended Master Plan 2031 so pending 5% residential plots for farmers whose land was acquired can be planned beside village settlements, potentially helping nearly 13,000 waiting allottees. Around 12,800 beneficiaries are still in the queue, farmers say.

stories.title: Bengaluru and NCR crack Asia-Pacific top 10 for rent growth
stories.summary: Business Standard, citing Knight Frank's Q3 2026 Asia-Pacific office report, says Bengaluru matched Tokyo at 11.5% prime rent growth while Delhi-NCR rose 5.4% and Mumbai 4%. Two Indian cities sit in the regional top 10. Hong Kong still led the pack at 17.1%.

stories.title: GCCs now drive up to 45% of India office demand, REIT chief says
stories.summary: Mindspace Business Parks REIT MD and CEO Ramesh Nair told ET that global capability centres account for about 40% to 45% of India's office demand and remain the biggest opportunity for REITs as more centres set up here. The tenants keep arriving with their own badges.

stories.title: Landmark Group commits ₹1,000 crore to Gurugram Landmark One
stories.summary: Landmark Group plans to invest about ₹1,000 crore to build Landmark One, a 2.1 million sq ft commercial project on Golf Course Extension Road, Gurugram, after raising ₹330 crore from SBI for phase one. A Dwarka Expressway mixed-use plan is also on the table.

stories.title: FabInvest puts ₹75 crore into HITEC City Grade A office
stories.summary: Fractional platform FabInvest fully funded ₹75 crore for a ground-plus-16 Grade A office in Hyderabad's HITEC City, its largest single-project cheque, taking AUM past ₹305 crore. Earlier deals were mostly residential tickets of ₹20 to ₹30 crore. Commercial just got a bigger wallet.

stories.title: Hong Kong, Brisbane, Tokyo, then Bengaluru on APAC rent league
stories.summary: CNBC-TV18's Knight Frank ranking for Q3 2026 puts Hong Kong first on prime office rent growth at 17.1%, Brisbane second at 12.1%, Tokyo third and Bengaluru fourth, both at 11.5%. India's Startup City is sharing a podium with places that charge for the view.

stories.title: Next CRE cycle is about experience and efficiency, not just sq ft
stories.summary: PropNews Time argues India's commercial real estate cycle is shifting toward workplace experience, utilisation and operating efficiency alongside classic leasing metrics. Square feet still matter. How people use them is the new KPI on the landlord slide.

stories.title: Anant Raj clears RERA for Estate One, eyes 357 MW of IT load
stories.summary: Anant Raj received Haryana RERA registration for The Estate One luxury project in Gurugram Sector 63A, with about 1.22 million sq ft of potential built-up area, while targeting 357 MW of data-centre IT load by FY2032. Launch timing and prices were not disclosed with the certificate.

stories.title: Anant Raj runs 28 MW now, plans Ashok Cloud listing path
stories.summary: Tele.net reports Anant Raj operates 28 MW of IT load at Manesar and Panchkula and wants 357 MW by FY32 across North and South India. In July 2026 it said it would separate data-centre and cloud services into Ashok Cloud for a separate listing. Power and property share a campus.

stories.title: Vikram Solar takes 5.7 lakh sq ft at Indospace Park Vallam II
stories.summary: Hindustan Times, citing Propstack filings, says Vikram Solar leased 5.73 lakh sq ft of industrial space at Indospace Park Vallam II in Chennai for five years at a total rent of ₹93 crore, with 5,04,606 sq ft of carpet area on the books.

stories.title: Power, not land, may decide India's next AI data-centre map
stories.summary: Express Computer argues that AI workloads are making reliable electricity the binding constraint for new Indian data centres, ahead of land, capital or raw compute. Operators now ask how fast a site can be powered, not only how fast it can be built.

stories.title: CBRE: dark stores and mother hubs to add 75 mn sq ft by 2030
stories.summary: CBRE's quick-commerce report projects about 75 million sq ft of logistics demand by 2030 as dark stores within two to three kilometres of shoppers, backed by larger mother hubs, chase 10 to 30 minute delivery. Urban warehousing is getting smaller and closer to the doorbell.

stories.title: Cushman expands Southwest data-centre bench with Mark Bauer
stories.summary: Cushman and Wakefield said Mark Bauer joined as executive vice chairman in Phoenix with a multi-tenant data-centre advisory team for tenants, landlords, developers and operators. Nearly three decades of digital infrastructure experience, now sitting in a Southwest platform that needs more megawatts.

stories.title: Nairobi prime offices hit 84.9% occupancy, rents still flat
stories.summary: Streamline Feed reports Nairobi prime office occupancy at 84.88% in June 2026, up from 81.58% six months earlier, while Grade A rents have not risen since June 2022. Yields of 8.5% to 9.5% sit below a 14.4% lending rate. Debt needs rent growth to work.

stories.title: Michigan AG challenges Google data-centre power deal approval
stories.summary: Law360 reports Michigan Attorney General Dana Nessel asked regulators to reopen approval of DTE Electric’s plan to serve a 1-gigawatt Google data centre near Detroit. Power deals for hyperscale sites now draw attorneys general as well as planners.

stories.title: Central projects pipeline hits ₹37.56 lakh crore across 1,853 works
stories.summary: Trade Brains cites September 2026 figures showing ₹37.56 lakh crore of ongoing Central Sector projects, led by transport and logistics at ₹20.07 lakh crore and energy at ₹11.04 lakh crore. Property markets watch the corridors. The pipeline is large enough to need its own map.

stories.title: B-Smile retenders two Bengaluru elevated corridors at lower costs
stories.summary: Bengaluru Smart Infrastructure Ltd invited fresh bids for elevated corridors from Minerva Circle to Hudson Circle and Shoolay Circle to St John's Hospital Road after cancelling October 19 tenders. Revised estimates are ₹511.4 crore and ₹515 crore, both below the earlier tags.

stories.title: Nagpur panel weighs waiving ₹40,000-a-day Smart City penalties
stories.summary: The Times of India reports a Nagpur review committee is inclined to waive ₹40,000 daily delay penalties on Smart City contractors who say tender caps are ₹20,000 and who cite land handover, utility shifting and monsoon issues. The penalty clause is having a second hearing.

stories.title: Andhra Pradesh fast-tracks Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor push
stories.summary: The Economic Times reports the Andhra Pradesh government is accelerating work on the Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor as part of a wider smart-push on industrial infrastructure. Corridor land and trunk services remain the quiet machinery behind warehouse demand maps.

stories.title: MP Urban Growth Conclave targets jobs and 15 new townships
stories.summary: Coverage of Madhya Pradesh's Urban Growth Conclave 2.0 says Chief Minister Mohan Yadav set targets around 20 lakh jobs and 15 townships as the state pitches urban expansion. Township counts are easy to announce. The services arrive later, with the water tanker.

stories.title: Indian metros need more public space, not only more towers
stories.summary: A Mint opinion argues Indian cities keep adding buildings and vehicles without enough places to gather, after disputes over protest sites in Delhi and Bengaluru. Real estate pipelines fill the skyline. Parks and plazas remain the scarce floor plate.

stories.title: Nagpur Metro builds 257m bridge 80ft above railway lines
stories.summary: The Times of India reports a 257-metre Metro bridge taking shape about 80 feet above railway lines in Nagpur, a civil package watched by corridor property markets nearby. Height clearances matter when trains refuse to move.

stories.title: Chennai Metro Phase II Arcot Road stations slip to March 2027
stories.summary: Six Metro stations on the Poonamallee to Vadapalani Arcot Road stretch of Chennai Metro Phase II are now aimed for March 2027, nearly ten months late, with Alapakkam to Saligramam still incomplete. Corridor property clocks watch the revised date.

stories.title: Delhi winter curbs spare some infrastructure sites from dust ban
stories.summary: Hindustan Times reports Delhi's winter action plan may ban most construction from 10 December to 20 January while major infrastructure projects keep exemptions, a dust loophole experts say will limit the clean-air effect. The skyline work continues under a different stamp.

stories.title: Allahabad HC orders demolition of two illegal Ghaziabad towers
stories.summary: Live Mint reports the Allahabad High Court ordered demolition of two illegal towers at a Ghaziabad society and imposed costs, tightening the line on unauthorised vertical additions. The judgment is for the builders who built first and filed later.

stories.title: Bombay HC quashes ₹9.27 lakh stamp duty on later conveyance
stories.summary: Bombay High Court set aside a ₹9.27 lakh stamp duty demand, holding a subsequent conveyance could not be treated as a fresh instrument in the disputed facts. Stamp offices sometimes invent a second sale. The court declined the encore.

stories.title: Uttar Pradesh proposes 0.5% stamp duty on company mergers
stories.summary: Prop News Time reports Uttar Pradesh has proposed a 0.5% stamp duty rate for company mergers and demergers, a carve-out watched by property-heavy restructurings. Deal lawyers will read the fine print before the valuation slides.

stories.title: Allahabad HC orders two Gulmohar Greens towers demolished
stories.summary: Coverage of the Allahabad High Court order says two illegal towers at Ghaziabad’s Gulmohar Greens must come down, with costs imposed on those who built without clear sanction. Vertical ambition met a horizontal judgment.

stories.title: India real estate PE falls 31% to $1.66 billion in Jan-Sep
stories.summary: Realty Plus reports private equity into Indian real estate dropped 31% to $1.66 billion in January to September 2026. Capital is still present. It is choosier about which towers get the term sheet.

stories.title: Vista Property eyes $34 million Fulton Market office deal
stories.summary: Yahoo Finance reports Vista Property is pursuing a Fulton Market office acquisition around $34 million. Another CBD asset changes hands while US office narratives stay noisy. The bid is quieter than the vacancy charts.

stories.title: Evergrande liquidators seal $513 million property stake sale
stories.summary: Law360 reports Evergrande liquidators agreed a $513 million deal to sell a property stake as the wind-down grinds on. The number is large. The developer story remains a cautionary footnote for cross-border credit committees.

stories.title: Morguard REIT Q3 watched for debt and earnings relief
stories.summary: Simply Wall St asks whether Morguard REIT’s latest quarter can ease debt concerns for investors tracking Canadian commercial trusts. REIT math is still rent, rate and refinance, in that anxious order.

stories.title: HousingWire rounds Q3 mortgage, REIT and homebuilder earnings
stories.summary: HousingWire summarises third-quarter 2026 results across mortgage lenders, brokerages, builders, listing portals and title firms, including PennyMac's $29 million profit print. The housing stack reports in the same week and argues about the same rates.

stories.title: NoBroker opens 5,500 sq ft interiors studio in Pune Kharadi
stories.summary: PropNews coverage says NoBroker opened a 5,500-square-foot home interiors experience centre in Pune's Kharadi, extending its interiors arm beyond the listing app. Brokers once measured with tape. The showroom now measures footfall.

stories.title: NoBroker Interiors plans two more Pune centres in 2027
stories.summary: NoBroker Interiors said its second Pune experience centre in Kharadi is open and that two more Pune locations are planned for 2027. The marketplace is building rooms you can walk through before you click buy.

stories.title: ImageDeep launches Houndlight solar AI camera for remote sites
stories.summary: Boston Real Estate Times reports ImageDeep launched Houndlight, a solar-powered AI security camera aimed at remote industrial and property sites. PropTech sometimes means another sensor on a pole that never asks for tea.

stories.title: Hiizzy CEO backs £116m UK digital property reform push
stories.summary: Coverage quotes Hiizzy’s CEO backing a £116 million UK property reform drive meant to cut red tape and speed digital home sales. PropTech loves a government that digitises the conveyancing pile.

stories.title: TCI MAX launches 53 Grade Winter Shield cement in Kashmir
stories.summary: Greater Kashmir reports TCI MAX has launched a 53 Grade Winter Shield cement line for Kashmir conditions, pitching cold-weather pours to local contractors. Winter builds need cement that does not sulk at the temperature.

stories.title: Orient Cement Q2 FY27 call focuses on volumes and pricing
stories.summary: Kalkine's note on Orient Cement's Q2 FY27 analyst call flags management discussion of volumes, pricing and near-term demand. Cement makers still narrate the same three slides. Investors still ask which one moved.

stories.title: Umrangso plant pushed as Assam's cement capacity story
stories.summary: Borok Times covers the Umrangso cement plant as a driver of Assam's production push, tying regional infrastructure demand to local grinding and clinker capacity. The Northeast's pours prefer shorter trucking distances.

stories.title: L&T maps expansion to double order book by 2031
stories.summary: ET Infra reports Larsen and Toubro has charted an expansion path aimed at doubling its order book by 2031, a signal watched by contractors and materials suppliers tied to big civil packages. The backlog target is large enough to need its own Gantt chart.

stories.title: Huaxin Building Materials lifts Q3 profit as revenue rises
stories.summary: Moomoo reports Huaxin Building Materials posted higher third-quarter profit with revenue up, another regional materials print watched by contractors who are still pricing cement and aggregates. Margins still begin at the kiln door.

stories.title: Green buildings open startup lanes across materials and tech
stories.summary: The Hans India reports growing startup activity around green buildings in India, from materials to monitoring, as developers chase certifications and lower operating loads. The pitch decks now mention embodied carbon between the amenity lists.

stories.title: SPA session flags net-zero pathways for campus and city projects
stories.summary: The New Indian Express covers a School of Planning and Architecture discussion on net-zero emissions in the built environment, linking design studios to operational energy targets. Students get the targets. Campuses still negotiate the electricity bill.

stories.title: Al Jalila Foundation building earns LEED Gold in Dubai
stories.summary: Gulf News reports the Al Jalila Foundation building received LEED Gold certification for its sustainability measures. Another institutional campus joins the certified list. The scorecard travels better than the cooling load.

stories.title: Forbes case for giving building materials a second life
stories.summary: A Forbes feature argues for reuse and second-life pathways for building materials as construction seeks lower embodied carbon. Demolition waste is reframed as inventory if someone measures it before the skip arrives.

stories.title: Green building materials firm may add 100 jobs in Brockton
stories.summary: Enterprise News reports a green building materials company could bring about 100 jobs to Brockton, tying local employment to low-carbon product lines. The factory floor is where the certificate becomes a payroll.

stories.title: Australian architects urge rethink for zero-carbon housing
stories.summary: The Australian Institute of Architects released Zero Carbon Housing Challenge findings analysing more than 330 homes and arguing smarter design, materials and renovation can cut footprints without always rebuilding. Net-zero housing starts with the brief, not the brochure.

stories.title: Cushman Marketbeat sketches Jakarta office and investment tone
stories.summary: Cushman and Wakefield's Jakarta Marketbeat for Q2 2026 updates occupancy, rents and investment appetite in Indonesia's capital. Southeast Asian office charts remain a useful foil for Indian GCC demand stories.

stories.title: UK Budget risks weighed for sovereign wealth and property
stories.summary: Bisnow reports industry concern that UK Budget measures could hit sovereign wealth appetite for real estate allocations across London and beyond. Policy slides move first. Transaction pipelines digest them a quarter later.

stories.title: Goldman sketches 2027 US housing outlook under higher mortgages
stories.summary: Goldman Sachs outlines a 2027 US housing view in which elevated mortgage rates keep weighing on volumes and prices. Affordability remains the slide with the smallest font and the longest arrow.

stories.title: UK buy-to-let landlords sell after years of tax rises
stories.summary: Bloomberg reports UK buy-to-let investors selling portfolios after years of successive tax rises, a supply story for rental markets watching landlord flight. The yield models were rewritten quietly by the Revenue.

stories.title: Autumn Budget 2026: housing measures in Chancellor Healey's box
stories.summary: The Negotiator rounds up what the UK Autumn Budget 2026 announced for the housing market, from tax tweaks to transaction expectations. Agents read the red box so clients do not have to.

stories.title: OBR sees UK house-price growth and transactions sliding
stories.summary: The Negotiator cites Office for Budget Responsibility claims that UK house-price growth and property transactions are set to slide after the Budget path. Forecasts rarely improve the weekend viewing slots for agents.

stories.title: Five analyst questions from JLL’s Q3 earnings call
stories.summary: StockStory lists the top five analyst questions from JLL's third-quarter earnings call, spanning leasing markets, capital markets desks and costs. Brokerage earnings calls remain a guided tour of everyone else's vacancy rates.
